I have never been to school, so I farm the way my mother taught me. This bean plot is small, only 0.15 hectares, and I plant it together with some maize or cassava. I will not buy chemical fertilizer for beans — it is too expensive and one bag is more than this small plot needs. Instead I will put a little compost and manure from behind my house, because the land is mine and I want to keep it good. I will use my own bean seed from last season, not the new seed in the packet. I will not spray chemicals or irrigate — we wait for the rains here in Mulanje, and those shop chemicals are for rich people with cash crops. My children and I will do all the work ourselves. We will spend about 20 days on this plot from planting to harvest, but I will not hire anyone because I do not have money for wages.
